asr.temperature: 0.0 with fallback through 1.0; default compression-ratio and log-prob gates

environment.tts: Gnani Timbre v2.5 (live, not used for scoring)
environment.snr_definition: active-speech RMS / noise RMS, measured per clip before the 8 kHz mu-law roundtrip

fixtures.source: Microsoft Edge TTS, synthetic Tamil/Tanglish scripts

policy.definition: Both raw and conditioned decodes are parsed. The sheet is pre-filled when both validate to the same four values, or when exactly one validates; otherwise the turn goes to readback or re-ask.

claim: Live Gnani Prisma v3.0 decoded the same frozen matrix. On 24 synthetic Tamil/Tanglish clips a single spectral front-end did not consistently fix noise (band+gate vs none: 14/24 vs 15/24 exact at 5 dB, 20/24 vs 20/24 clean), so the shipped line listens twice: it pre-filled 20/24 clean pours correctly with 0 silent errors, 16/24 at 5 dB with 0 silent errors (raw alone: 15 correct, 0 silent errors), and 12/24 at 0 dB with 0 silent errors (raw: 10, 0 silent errors); everything else went to readback or re-ask (our own synthetic clips, not field data; n=24 per cell, Wilson 95% CIs in the table). Slot exactness is the comparable metric here; WER against the Tamil scripts is not comparable to Tanglish transcripts and is not used in this claim.
caveats: Live provider check only; the shipped 192-run benchmark and its claim remain the local faster-whisper run.
24 synthetic TTS clips per condition; no field or real-farmer audio.
Prisma returns Tanglish; the slot compiler is applied unchanged, so exactness measures parse+validation, not raw verbatim ASR.
WER against the Tamil reference is script-mismatched and is not a headline metric for this arm.
Calls are metered and were made with a participant-supplied key; no key material is stored in this file.
